newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - May 26.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - May 26.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

BERLIN - The federal cartel office says it is checking if the frequent flier programme of Deutsche Lufthansa AG, Miles & More, violates free trade laws. It says the Eurowings airline lodged a complaint against the programme two weeks ago.
(Reuter)

HAMBURG - Deutsche Telekom chief executive Ron Sommer is becoming increasingly annoyed by the advertising campaigns of the former monopoly's upstart competitors. Before a soccer match on April 30 against Ukraine in Bremen, Telekom tried to put pressure on the organisers to refuse to run an ad by telecommunications company Otelo. (Der Spiegel)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

HAMBURG - For what is reported to be over 100 million marks ($60 million), private station Pro Sieben has bought the rights to several Hollywood films from Telepool, which is owned by several local public broadcasters. The deal is for 60 percent of an exclusive output deal with Dreamworks Studios. (Der Spiegel)

WALLDORF - Chief executive of publishing company Suhrkamp, Siegfried Unseld, wants to buy the 50 percent shares in the company offered by Swiss businessman Andreas Reinhart, Unseld tells Der Spiegel. The two have already already agreed on a basic price range. (Kress)

BONN - The federal government needs to control the burgeoning markets of teleshopping and purchases over the Internet, television and other electronic media, says deputy SPD chairwoman Herta Daeubler-Gmelin. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
INGOLSTADT - Carmaker Audi, a unit of Volkswagen AG, says it is recalling 15,000 of its A3, A4 and A6 cars for repairs to the front seat safety belts. (Reuter)
STUTTGART - Daimler-Benz AG says that it is confident its disagreements with the Chinese governement over a proposed minivan plan can be resolved and the project will mover forward. (Reuter)
BREMEN - Coffee roaster Eduscho GmbH & Co KG says it will raise the price of four of its seven roasted coffee products by 1.50 marks per 500 grams on average, with effect from May 26.
(Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Consumer prices increased somewhat more sharply in May than in the previous few months, based on the latest reports of individual states. (Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung)

DUESSELDORF - Engineering group Mannesmann AG says its first-quarter sales rose 15 percent to 8.1 billion marks, driven by a 69 percent rise in telecommunications revenues to 1.4 billion marks. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:

WALLDORF - Heiko Haenler and Gerold Denker, managing directors of the Berlin advertising agency Die Bruecke, have left that agency to start a new one in Berlin. Die Bruecke is now under the leadership of founders Heiko Mehnert and Michael Friedberg.
(Kress)
WALLDORF - William Cullen and Harald Lindloff are the new chief executives of Motorola Electronic GmbH in Wiesbaden. (Kress)
WALLDORF - Peter Mayer will become a member of the board of
brewer Freiberger Brauhaus AG and will take over responsibility for marketing and distribution. (Kress)
Deborah Cole, Berlin Newsroom, 49-30-203-98114
